title: Controlling soil pollution
summary: Soil pollution is the presence of harmful substances in soil. Safe farming and waste practices keep soil healthy.
body:
## What pollutes soil?

**Soil pollution** happens when harmful substances get into the soil and harm plants, animals and people.

| Cause | Example |
|---|---|
| **Plastics and polythene** | Do not rot; block water and roots |
| **Agrochemicals** | Too much fertiliser, pesticides and herbicides |
| **Oil and fuel** | Spills from machines and garages |
| **Batteries and e-waste** | Release heavy metals like lead and mercury |
| **Untreated sewage** | Spreads germs |
| **Burning rubbish** | Leaves toxic ash |

## Controlling soil pollution at home

- **Reduce, reuse, recycle** plastics. Carry a reusable shopping bag.
- **Separate waste**: organic waste to compost; plastics, glass and metals for recycling.
- Use **organic manure** instead of too much chemical fertiliser.
- Follow the label: use **the right amount** of pesticide, at the right time.
- Store chemicals safely and never pour leftovers on the ground.
- Take old batteries and phones to **e-waste collection points**.

## Being responsible

Healthy soil grows healthy food. Every family and farmer has a part to play.
activities:
1. Survey your home compound and list every soil pollutant you find.
2. Set up two bins at home: organic and non-organic waste.
3. Read the label on a pesticide or fertiliser bag with an adult. Note the safety instructions.
reflection: Which one change can your family make this week to reduce soil pollution?

Old batteries should be...
options: Taken to an e-waste collection point

strand: Foundations of Creative Arts and Sports
sub_strand: Introduction to Creative Arts and Sports
title: What are Creative Arts and Sports?
summary: Creative Arts and Sports brings together visual arts, performing arts and sports, which are closely linked.
body:
## Categories

| Category | Includes |
|---|---|
| **Visual arts** | Drawing, painting, sculpture, pottery, weaving, photography, graphic design |
| **Performing arts** | Music, dance, drama, poetry recitation, film |
| **Sports** | Athletics, football, volleyball, netball, swimming, games |

## How they are related

The categories support each other:

- A **football match** has music and dance from the fans, and a designed **jersey and logo** (visual arts).
- A **drama** needs **costumes and stage props** (visual arts) and **fitness** for movement (sports).
- **Traditional dances** like *Isukuti* combine music, movement and decorated costumes.
- All of them need **creativity, discipline, teamwork and practice**.

## Why we learn it

- Expresses our **culture and ideas**
- Keeps us **healthy and fit**
- Builds **talent** that can become a **career** — artists, musicians, athletes, designers, coaches
- Brings communities together at festivals and games
activities:
1. Make a chart with three columns — visual arts, performing arts and sports — and list at least four activities under each.
2. Choose one event, like a wedding or a school sports day, and show how all three categories appear in it.
3. Name a Kenyan musician, artist and athlete you admire.
reflection: Which category do you enjoy most, and how could it link to the other two?

Drama and dance are examples of...
Which shows a link between sports and visual arts?
options: A designed team jersey and logo

title: Polite introductions
summary: We use polite expressions when we introduce ourselves and others, and show respect through our words and manners.
body:
## Introducing yourself

- *"Good morning. My name is Amina Otieno. I am a Grade 7 learner at Mji Mpya Junior School."*
- *"Hello, I'm Brian. Nice to meet you."*

## Introducing others

Introduce the **younger person to the older**, or the **guest to the host**:

- *"Mr. Kamau, may I introduce my friend Wanjiru? Wanjiru, this is Mr. Kamau, our class teacher."*
- *"Mum, I'd like you to meet Hassan. He is in my class."*

## Polite responses

| When | Say |
|---|---|
| Meeting someone | *"Pleased to meet you."* / *"Nice to meet you."* |
| Asking a name | *"May I know your name, please?"* |
| Leaving | *"It was nice meeting you."* |

## Respectful behaviour

- **Stand up** when an older person or visitor is introduced.
- Make **eye contact** and **smile**.
- Offer a **handshake** where it is the custom.
- Use **titles**: Mr., Mrs., Ms., Dr., Madam, Sir.
- **Listen** — remember the person's name and use it.
activities:
1. Introduce yourself to the class or family in three sentences.
2. Role-play introducing a friend to your parent using a polite expression.
3. Write a short dialogue where a visitor is introduced to your head teacher.
reflection: How do polite introductions help you make a good first impression?

quiz.question: Which is a polite response when introduced?
When introducing, we usually introduce...
options: The younger person to the older
The older person to the younger

quiz.question: Which shows respect during an introduction?
options: Standing up and making eye contact

quiz.question: Which is a polite way to ask a name?
options: May I know your name, please?

title: Welcome to Integrated Science
summary: Integrated Science brings together biology, chemistry and physics to explain the world around us.
body:
## What is Integrated Science?

**Science** is the study of the natural world through **observation and experiments**. In Junior School, Integrated Science combines three branches:

| Branch | Studies | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Biology** | Living things | How plants make food, how our body works |
| **Chemistry** | Substances and how they change | Why iron rusts, mixing and separating |
| **Physics** | Matter, energy and forces | Electricity, light, how a bicycle moves |

Many topics use all three — for example, **cooking** involves heat (physics), chemical changes in food (chemistry) and nutrition (biology).

## Science in daily life

- **Health**: vaccines, clean water, medicines
- **Agriculture**: better seeds, safe pesticides, irrigation
- **Energy**: solar panels, electricity, cooking gas
- **Communication**: phones, radio, internet
- **Environment**: understanding climate and conserving resources

## Careers in science

Doctors, nurses, engineers, pharmacists, agronomists, laboratory technicians, meteorologists, veterinary officers and many more.

## How scientists work

They **observe**, ask a **question**, make a **guess (hypothesis)**, **test** it with an experiment, and draw a **conclusion**.
activities:
1. List five things you used today that came from science.
2. Interview someone with a science-based job about what they do.
3. Ask a question about something at home (e.g. why milk goes sour) and suggest how to test your answer.
reflection: Which science career interests you, and why?

title: Kusikiliza na kujibu mazungumzo
summary: Mazungumzo mazuri yanahitaji kusikiliza kwa makini na kujibu kwa adabu na kwa ufasaha.
body:
## Vipengele vya kusikiliza

Msikilizaji mzuri:

- **Humtazama** msemaji na kutulia.
- **Hasumbui** wala kukatiza mazungumzo.
- **Huonyesha ishara** za kusikiliza: kutikisa kichwa, kutabasamu.
- **Huzingatia** ujumbe mkuu na maelezo muhimu.
- **Huuliza swali** pale ambapo hakuelewa.

## Vipengele vya kujibu

Mjibuji mzuri:

- **Hujibu kulingana na swali** — hatoki nje ya mada.
- Hutumia **lugha ya adabu**: *tafadhali, asante, samahani*.
- **Huzungumza kwa sauti inayosikika** na kwa utaratibu.
- **Husubiri zamu yake** kabla ya kuzungumza.
- Hutumia **lugha ya mwili** inayofaa.

## Mfano wa mazungumzo

**Mwalimu:** *Halima, ulifanya nini wikendi?*
**Halima:** *Nilimsaidia mama sokoni Jumamosi, mwalimu. Jumapili nilisoma kitabu cha hadithi.*
**Mwalimu:** *Vizuri sana! Kitabu kilihusu nini?*
**Halima:** *Kilihusu mvulana aliyepanda miti kijijini kwao.*
activities:
1. Fanya mazungumzo na mzazi kuhusu siku yako. Zingatia vipengele vya kusikiliza.
2. Andika mazungumzo mafupi kati ya mnunuzi na muuzaji sokoni.
3. Igiza mazungumzo hayo na rafiki darasani au nyumbani.
reflection: Ni kipengele kipi cha kusikiliza unachohitaji kukiboresha?

title: Whole numbers up to hundreds of millions
summary: We read, write and round off very large numbers, and classify numbers as even, odd and prime.
body:
## Place value

In **583,406,129**:

| Hundred millions | Ten millions | Millions | Hundred thousands | Ten thousands | Thousands | Hundreds | Tens | Ones |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 8 | 3 | 4 | 0 | 6 | 1 | 2 | 9 |

- Total value of 8 = **80,000,000** (eighty million)
- In words: *five hundred and eighty-three million, four hundred and six thousand, one hundred and twenty-nine*

## Rounding off

To the nearest **million**, look at the hundred-thousands digit:

- 583,**4**06,129 → **583,000,000** (4 is less than 5, round down)
- 583,**7**06,129 → **584,000,000** (round up)

## Even, odd and prime numbers

| Type | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Even** | Divisible by 2 | 2, 14, 100 |
| **Odd** | Not divisible by 2 | 3, 15, 99 |
| **Prime** | Has exactly two factors: 1 and itself | 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 |

**1 is not prime** (it has only one factor), and **2 is the only even prime**.

## Operations

A county receives **KSh 345,000,000** and spends **KSh 128,500,000** on health. Left: 345,000,000 − 128,500,000 = **KSh 216,500,000**.
activities:
1. Write the total value of each digit in 207,915,384.
2. List all prime numbers between 1 and 50.
3. Find a big number in a newspaper (a budget or population). Round it to the nearest million.
reflection: Why do governments use rounded numbers when they talk about budgets?

title: What is Pre-Technical Studies?
summary: Pre-Technical Studies introduces skills and tools used in technical jobs, from woodwork to computing.
body:
## Components of Pre-Technical Studies

Pre-Technical Studies brings together:

- **Safety** at work and at home
- **Materials** — wood, metal, plastics, fabrics, and their uses
- **Tools and equipment** — measuring, cutting, joining
- **Technical drawing** — showing objects on paper so others can make them
- **Computing and ICT** — computers, data and digital skills
- **Entrepreneurship** — turning skills into a business

## Its role in daily life

- **Fixing things**: a broken chair, a leaking tap, a loose door handle
- **Making things**: a shoe rack, a sign board, a simple stool
- **Using technology** safely: phones, computers, mobile money
- **Saving money** by repairing instead of buying new

## Careers

Engineers, electricians, plumbers, carpenters, mechanics, welders, architects, ICT technicians, fashion designers and many more. **Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET)** colleges train young people for these careers.

## Skills you build

Problem solving, creativity, accuracy in measuring, teamwork and working safely.
activities:
1. List five tools used at home and say what each is used for.
2. Find something broken at home that could be repaired. Explain how you would fix it.
3. Talk to a local fundi (mechanic, carpenter or tailor) about their work.
reflection: Which technical career would you like to explore, and why?

title: Knowing myself: abilities, interests and goals
summary: Exploring your abilities and interests helps you set goals and choose a career that fits you.
body:
## Abilities and interests

- **Abilities** are things you are good at: solving maths problems, drawing, running, talking to people.
- **Interests** are things you enjoy: reading, fixing bicycles, caring for animals, music.

The best careers often combine **what you are good at** and **what you enjoy**.

## Discovering yourself

Ask yourself:

- Which subjects do I enjoy most?
- What do people often ask me to help with?
- What could I do for hours without getting bored?

## Setting SMART goals

A good goal is **SMART**:

| Letter | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **S** | Specific | Improve my Mathematics mark |
| **M** | Measurable | From 55% to 70% |
| **A** | Achievable | By practising 30 minutes a day |
| **R** | Relevant | I want to be an engineer |
| **T** | Time-bound | By the end of term |

## Careers related to Social Studies

Teacher, lawyer, journalist, diplomat, tour guide, historian, geographer, social worker, politician, urban planner and economist.
activities:
1. List three abilities and three interests you have.
2. Write one SMART goal for this term.
3. Ask two adults what they wanted to be at your age and what they do now.
reflection: How does knowing yourself help you make better choices?
